evidence.description: The event enum defines only an empty-string case.
The empty raw value is passed directly to the SDK as the event name.

candidates.explanation: The only representable CustomEvent has an empty raw value, and logCustomEvent forwards that value directly to Braze. Consequently, this public logging API cannot emit a valid, meaningfully named custom event.
candidates.title: Custom events can only have an empty name

evidence.description: Every enabled call initializes Braze and launches a new task without an initialization-state guard.
Initialization unconditionally constructs and assigns a new SDK instance and reinstalls its delegates and presenter.

candidates.explanation: initialize() has no check for an existing Braze instance or initialization already in progress. Each enabled invocation replaces the service's SDK instance and starts another untracked notification-registration and consent task. Repeated calls therefore duplicate initialization work and can overlap the asynchronous notification flows.
candidates.title: Repeated initialization replaces the active SDK instance

evidence.description: The status refresh occurs only after the throwing authorization request succeeds.
The automatic registration path suppresses errors from the consent request.

candidates.explanation: requestAuthorization can throw, in which case execution exits before notificationAuthorizationStatus is refreshed. The cached status is therefore not always updated as the method claims. In the automatic refresh path, the same error is discarded with try?, leaving no indication that the request and subsequent status refresh did not complete.
candidates.title: Authorization errors skip the cached-status refresh
